item.description:
Sukoon 1.6.6 — the adhan panel's buttons now actually work.

  • Stop and Dismiss respond to the whole button — the round controls on the adhan panel only registered clicks on the thin ring around them and on the small icon itself, so most clicks landing squarely inside them did nothing. After the adhan, where Dismiss is the only control, the panel could feel completely stuck. The same fix applies to every outlined button elsewhere, including the dropdowns in Settings, whose chevron was not clickable at all.
  • Your music pauses for the adhan, then comes back — new in Settings › Adhan, on by default. Whatever is playing — Music, Spotify, a video — is paused when the adhan starts and resumed when it ends, and the panel tells you which app it paused. If nothing is playing, nothing is touched.
  • Muted in a meeting no longer means a full-volume adhan — “Silence adhan during calls” previously watched only the microphone, so being muted — or presenting, having never unmuted — could let the adhan play into the room. Sukoon now also recognises a conferencing app that is holding your speakers, and says so.
  • At home on macOS 26 and later — the menu-bar icon stays legible against the transparent menu bar while the adhan plays, and corners throughout the app follow the rounder system chrome. Nothing changes on macOS 14 and 15.

Sukoon 1.6.5 — the day timeline comes to the widget.

  • The signature timeline, now on the large widget — the sun travels the day between Fajr and Isha, exactly as in the app's popover, replacing the plain progress bar.

Sukoon 1.6.4 — the widget release. The desktop widget now genuinely mirrors the app.

  • The widget follows the app by default — city AND calculation method. It used to default to Mecca with the Umm al-Qura method regardless of your settings, so its times could disagree with the menu bar by half an hour or more. If you added a widget before this update, open Edit Widget once and set City and Calculation Method to "Same as Sukoon app".
  • Rebuilt widget layout — no more text cut off at the edges, no truncated times, a countdown you can read from across the room, and the Hijri date and iqama time on every size.
  • Widget and app can no longer disagree — both now compute prayer times through one shared code path, verified by tests across every method, madhab, and high-latitude combination.
  • Sturdier refresh — a slow network connection could previously stall the app's location refresh; lookups no longer stack up.

Sukoon 1.6.3 — a correctness release. Times, the adhan, and the widget now agree with each other, and every label meets contrast standards.

  • The widget matches the app — it was calculating with its own method (Umm al-Qura) instead of yours, so its times could differ from the menu bar by half an hour or more. Widgets now follow the app's method, madhab, adjustments and accent. If you already have a widget on your desktop, open Edit Widget once and set Calculation Method to "Same as Sukoon app".
  • Cities abroad keep their own clock — a saved city in another timezone showed its prayer times in your local clock, which made the monthly timetable unusable for it. Times, the timetable and the widget now read in the city's own time.
  • No more late adhan after sleep — if your Mac slept through a prayer, the adhan could play in full hours later when you opened the lid. It now stays quiet once the moment has passed.
  • Fajr is no longer missed overnight — nothing was scheduled past Isha, so a Mac that slept before midnight woke to no Fajr adhan and no notification. Tomorrow's prayers are scheduled ahead now.
  • The adhan stops being silenced all day — background audio tools kept the "microphone in use" check permanently on. Sukoon now looks at which app is really capturing and names it ("Silenced — Zoom is using your microphone"), and the panel dismisses itself.
  • Mute stops the adhan that's playing — the bell used to only mute the next one.
  • Menu bar tells the truth — it announced the prayer up to a minute early, and Arabic now gets its own hour/minute letters instead of "h" and "m".
  • Readable everywhere — section labels and widget text sat below the accessibility contrast minimum in both light and dark modes. Every label now clears it.
  • Clearer statistics — the 14-day chart shows one mark per prayer, so a missed prayer is visible at a glance; the 12-week grid finally has weekday labels and a key; and the Qibla figures line up.
  • Widget polish — the Accent setting finally does something, the progress bar moves between prayers instead of freezing, and after Isha it no longer highlights this morning's Fajr.
  • Better Turkish, Urdu, Indonesian and French — countdown headings, the "mark as prayed" button, event countdowns and dates were falling back to English or reading ungrammatically.
  • Streaks survive the clocks changing — your longest streak reset at daylight-saving transitions.

Sukoon 1.6.1 — a redesigned day timeline.

  • Every prayer is labeled again — 1.6 could hide Maghrib's name on the timeline; sorry about that.
  • Five evenly-spaced stations — Fajr through Isha each get equal room, in Arabic and English alike, so labels never crowd or overlap. The sun still tracks real time as it travels toward the next prayer.

Sukoon 1.6 — location accuracy and first-run fixes, straight from user feedback.

  • City search loads as you type — no more pressing Return and wondering; the magnifier works too.
  • Exact city out of the box — first-run setup now uses on-device Location Services (with your permission), so Dubai no longer shows up as Abu Dhabi. When the approximate mode is in use, Sukoon says so and points to the fix.
  • The onboarding Allow button always works — if macOS already blocked notifications, it now takes you straight to System Settings with clear steps instead of doing nothing.
  • Travel suggestions as notifications — when your country's prayer-time convention differs, you'll know without opening the popover.
  • Cleaner Arabic — no more duplicated English + Arabic prayer names when the app is in Arabic, and timeline labels no longer overlap on short evenings.

Sukoon 1.6.2 — now also on the Mac App Store! This update brings both channels in sync.

  • A dedication — Sukoon is, and will always be, free: a sadaqah jariyah from its maker. The welcome screen and Settings now carry this dedication and a request for dua.
  • Gentler onboarding — permissions are clearly optional, buttons say Continue, and Get Started always works.
  • Clearer location feedback — Settings shows your selected city with a checkmark; the permission prompt can no longer appear behind other windows.
  • Timeline label fix, refreshed support page at mindmints.ai/sukoon/support, and polish throughout.

Sukoon 1.5 — a polish release from a full UI/UX audit. 31 fixes.

  • Accent colors now work — pick any of the six accents and the whole app follows, in light and dark.
  • The adhan panel no longer steals your typing focus — it appears quietly without switching apps.
  • Honest qibla — clear "° from North" bearing with a practical hint, no fake compass claims.
  • VoiceOver & keyboard access for all controls, better small-text contrast, larger click targets.
  • 12/24-hour clock follows your macOS setting, everywhere including widgets.
  • Popover density setting works, prayer names localized in the main list, save cities with a star, download retry, undo-aware prayer logging, dark-mode fixes, persistent tasbih, and more.

Sukoon 1.4 — the biggest update yet, and the first notarized release (no more security warnings on install).

  • Meeting-aware adhan — silences itself when your microphone is in use, so the adhan never interrupts a call.
  • Mark prayed from the notification — log a prayer without opening anything.
  • Tap-to-log on widgets — check off prayers right on the widget.
  • After-adhan dua — the panel lingers with the dua between adhan and iqama.
  • Travel mode — suggests the locally-used calculation method when you change country.
  • Precise location (opt-in) — exact times via Location Services; your location never leaves your Mac.
  • Shortcuts & Siri — Next Prayer, Log Prayer, and automation recipes.
  • Four new languages — اردو, Türkçe, Bahasa Indonesia, Français.
  • Year in review — yearly stats with a shareable card, plus live adhan phrase tracking, offline fallback, and better first-run screens.
Sukoon 1.3 — Arabic widget faces (widgets now follow the app language), plus automatic silent updates via Sparkle.
